hook.en: Accounts are closed and profits distributed. Then someone notices interest on capital was never allowed. Do we redo the whole year?
hook.kn: ಖಾತೆಗಳು ಮುಕ್ತಾಯವಾಗಿ ಲಾಭ ಹಂಚಿಕೆಯಾಗಿದೆ. ನಂತರ ಬಂಡವಾಳದ ಬಡ್ಡಿ ನೀಡಿಲ್ಲ ಎಂದು ಗೊತ್ತಾಗುತ್ತದೆ. ಇಡೀ ವರ್ಷ ಮತ್ತೆ ಮಾಡಬೇಕೇ?

narration.en: Accounts are closed and profits distributed. Then someone notices interest on capital was never allowed. Do we redo the whole year? No — one adjustment entry is enough.

title.en: Prepare an adjustment table for omitted items

say.en: Accounts are closed and profits distributed. Then someone notices interest on capital was never allowed. Do we redo the whole year? No, one adjustment entry is enough. In this lesson: Prepare an adjustment table for omitted items.
Pass a single adjustment entry.

body.en: List what each partner should have been credited (for example, omitted interest on capital) and debited (omitted interest on drawings). The net omitted amount would have reduced or increased the profit already distributed, so reverse it in the profit sharing ratio. The net figure for each partner shows who is to be credited and who debited; one entry between partners' capital (or current) accounts corrects everything.
body.kn: ಪ್ರತಿ ಪಾಲುದಾರನಿಗೆ ಜಮಾ ಮತ್ತು ಖರ್ಚು ಆಗಬೇಕಾಗಿದ್ದ ಮೊತ್ತಗಳನ್ನು ಪಟ್ಟಿ ಮಾಡಿ, ಹಂಚಿದ ಲಾಭವನ್ನು ಅನುಪಾತದಲ್ಲಿ ಹಿಂತಿರುಗಿಸಿ. ನಿವ್ವಳ ಮೊತ್ತಕ್ಕೆ ಪಾಲುದಾರರ ಖಾತೆಗಳ ನಡುವೆ ಒಂದು ನಮೂದು ಸಾಕು.

title.en: Correct an omitted interest on capital

caption.en: Interest on capital was left out, and the whole profit was already shared. Each partner should get his interest, but the same total must come back out of profit in the profit sharing ratio. Only the net difference is adjusted.
caption.kn: ಬಂಡವಾಳ ಬಡ್ಡಿ ಬಿಟ್ಟುಹೋಗಿದೆ, ಲಾಭ ಈಗಾಗಲೇ ಹಂಚಲಾಗಿದೆ. ಪ್ರತಿಯೊಬ್ಬರಿಗೂ ಬಡ್ಡಿ ಸಿಗಬೇಕು, ಅದೇ ಮೊತ್ತ ಲಾಭ ಹಂಚಿಕೆ ಅನುಪಾತದಲ್ಲಿ ಹಿಂತಿರುಗಬೇಕು. ನಿವ್ವಳ ವ್ಯತ್ಯಾಸ ಮಾತ್ರ ಹೊಂದಿಸಲಾಗುತ್ತದೆ.

problem.en: A and B share profits 3:2 with capitals ₹1,00,000 and ₹50,000. After the accounts were closed, it was found that interest on capital at 10% p.a. was not allowed. Pass the adjustment entry.

steps.en: Excess profit already given, reversed 3:2: A ₹9,000 Dr, B ₹6,000 Dr.
Entry: B's Capital A/c Dr ₹1,000 To A's Capital A/c ₹1,000.

answer.en: B's Capital A/c Dr ₹1,000; To A's Capital A/c ₹1,000

narration.en: Let us work this out together, step by step. A and B share profits 3:2 with capitals ₹1,00,000 and ₹50,000. After the accounts were closed, it was found that interest on capital at 10% p.a. was not allowed. Pass the adjustment entry.

say.en: Let us work this out together, step by step. A and B share profits 3:2 with capitals 1,00,000 rupees and 50,000 rupees. After the accounts were closed, it was found that interest on capital at 10 percent p.a. was not allowed. Pass the adjustment entry.
Interest omitted: A 10,000, rupees B 5,000 rupees (total 15,000 rupees).
Excess profit already given, reversed 3:2: A 9,000 rupees Dr, B 6,000 rupees Dr.
Net: A plus 10,000 minus 9,000 equals 1,000 rupees Cr; B plus 5,000 minus 6,000 equals 1,000 rupees Dr.
Entry: B's Capital A over c Dr 1,000 rupees To A's Capital A over c 1,000 rupees.
So the answer is B's Capital A over c Dr 1,000 rupees; To A's Capital A over c 1,000 rupees.
